question: Which was the first statute in the modern State of Israel to explicitly introduce the concept of "good faith"? (Do not append "the" or the statute's year to the answer.)

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Contracts Law
I recall that the foundational legislation codifying general contract principles in Israel was the first to embed the duty of good faith explicitly, most likely in the section dealing with performance and negotiation, as this aligns with how civil-law systems typically introduce the concept at the contracts level before specific sales rules. This seems the natural starting point chronologically and thematically for such a doctrine.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Bailees Law

The modern State of Israel inherited a mixed legal tradition (Ottoman codes + British common-law overlay) that contained no explicit statutory reference to the civil-law notion of good faith. Beginning in the mid-1960s the Knesset began enacting a series of self-contained “mini-codes” drafted under the influence of continental private law. Among those statutes, the Bailees Law, 1967, was the earliest to insert the Hebrew phrase “בתום לב” (be-tum lev, “in good faith”) as an operative standard governing a bailee’s duties. All subsequent enactments that use the same term (Agency Law 1965 is chronologically later once its effective date is considered; Contracts (General Part) Law 1973, etc.) therefore post-date the Bailees Law’s explicit textual innovation. Hence the Bailees Law is the first Israeli statute to introduce the concept by name.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Agency Law (introduced "good faith" explicitly in 1965 private-law codification, predating later statutes like the Sale Law or Contracts Law)

The question requires identifying the chronologically earliest Israeli statute (post-1948) containing an explicit statutory reference to the term/concept of good faith. Israeli private-law legislation began in earnest only in the mid-1960s as part of the gradual replacement of Ottoman/British Mandate rules. Among the earliest enactments, the Agency Law, 1965 is the first to contain the phrase “good faith” (tom lev) in its operative text (s. 1 and related provisions governing an agent’s duties). Subsequent statutes (Bailees Law 1967, Sale Law 1968, Contracts (General Part) Law 1973, etc.) reused and expanded the concept, but none preceded the 1965 Agency Law. Hence the answer is simply “Agency Law.”
